Agency View vs. Location / Sub-account View
One of the most important distinctions in client operations
AGENCY VIEW
Agency-level operations: manage client locations/accounts, agency settings, snapshots or account administration where available, and agency-level configuration.Ask: “Am I managing the platform/client account, or working inside one business?”
LOCATION / SUB-ACCOUNT VIEW
Work inside one client business. Features and data here belong to that location: contacts, conversations, calendars, pipelines, workflows, sites, and business settings (subject to plan and permissions).

Dashboard component breakdown
Read the dashboard before editing it
Dashboard selector
Switch between dashboards available to you; search, add, pin or open shared dashboards depending on permissions.
Date range
Controls the period used by dashboard widgets; some widgets may have their own overrides.
Filters
Dashboard-level filters and filter pills can narrow the data displayed.
Widgets
Metric cards, charts, tables or other visual summaries.
Edit mode
Allows changes to dashboard layout/widgets, where permitted.
Action menu
Dashboard-specific actions may be available from a menu.
Quick Filters
A side panel or control for dashboard filter configuration, depending on UI.
AI summary
May offer a summary of dashboard data when available.
6

Dashboard: view mode vs edit mode
Know the difference before making changes
VIEW MODE
Use this to review business activity.• Change date range and filters• Read widgets and trends• Avoid changing layout• Use metrics to identify a client issue
EDIT MODE
Use this to customize the dashboard.• Reorder widgets• Add or remove widgets• Change title/theme or layout options where available• Save and confirm the change

Dashboard editing workflow
Safe workflow before changing a client dashboard
1. Confirm you are in the correct location/sub-account.
2. Open the correct dashboard. Record its current name and layout.
3. Confirm the client’s objective: what should the dashboard answer?
4. Enter Edit mode.
5. Add, remove, rearrange, or configure widgets as needed.
6. Review filters and date ranges—avoid accidentally hiding data.
7. Save/exit editing.
8. Reopen or refresh and verify the change.
9. Send the client a concise change summary.

Finding features when the menu is unfamiliar
Search, All Products, Recents, Pinned and breadcrumbs may be available in redesigned navigation
SEARCH
Use search to locate a product/page by name when available. Verify that the result is the feature—not a settings page or help result.
ALL PRODUCTS
Browse the product directory when you do not know the exact feature name. Grouping and availability can vary.
RECENTS / PINNED
Use recently visited or pinned items to speed up repeated work. Do not assume these shortcuts are visible in every UI version.

Navigation customization: important distinction
Visibility is not the same as permission
Navigation customization controls how products/groups appear in the sidebar.
Hiding a product does not necessarily disable it or revoke access.
User permissions control what a user can access or do.
Navigation changes may be shared across a sub-account layout, not just one person.
Confirm plan eligibility and scope before customizing.
Document the original layout so you can restore it if needed.
15

Dashboard troubleshooting checklist
Use this before reporting that “the dashboard is broken”
Wrong location/sub-account?
Wrong dashboard selected?
Date range too narrow or incorrect?
Dashboard-level filter applied?
Widget-level filter or comparison range overriding the dashboard?
Widget deleted or not configured?
User permission issue?
Data not yet populated or delayed?
Refresh/reopen and verify. Capture evidence and report findings.
16

Account navigation safety rules
Small navigation mistakes can create client-impacting changes
Check location name before every change.
Do not change navigation, permissions, integrations or settings just to “see what happens” in a live client account.
Use a test location when possible.
Ask for approval before changing shared layouts or account-wide settings.
Record current state before editing.
Test the result with the intended user role if access changes are involved.
Never assume a hidden menu item means the feature is disabled.

Client Mission 01 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“I can’t find the Contacts menu anymore.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Diagnose navigation visibility, customized layout, UI version, and permissions.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm location. 2) Inspect sidebar/search/All Products. 3) Check whether navigation is customized or item hidden. 4) Verify user permissions. 5) Restore/show item only with approval. 6) Test access.
EXPECTED RESULT
Contacts is visible or the user’s permission issue is identified; explain the difference between visibility and access.
18

Client Mission 02 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“I’m seeing the wrong business account.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
User may be in the wrong location.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Read current location name. 2) Open location/account selector. 3) Select requested client. 4) Confirm business identity before working. 5) Reopen requested feature.
EXPECTED RESULT
Correct client location confirmed; no changes made to the wrong account.
19

Client Mission 03 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Can you put our most-used tools at the top?”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Navigation reorganization request.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm exact items and desired order. 2) Check plan/UI eligibility. 3) Open navigation Edit. 4) Reorder items/groups. 5) Review scope. 6) Save and verify with client user.
EXPECTED RESULT
Approved tools appear in requested order; document shared-layout impact.
20

Client Mission 04 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Hide the Payments menu from my receptionist.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Potential permissions request disguised as hiding.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Clarify whether they want it hidden or access restricted. 2) Check role/permissions. 3) If restriction is intended, use permission controls—not only navigation hide. 4) Apply approved change. 5) Test as receptionist role.
EXPECTED RESULT
Payment access is appropriately restricted, not merely hidden from the sidebar.
21

Client Mission 05 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“My dashboard numbers are wrong.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Date range, filters, widget configuration, or data scope.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm location and dashboard. 2) Check date range. 3) Inspect dashboard filters. 4) Inspect widget filters. 5) Compare with source records. 6) Refresh and document discrepancy.
EXPECTED RESULT
Identify whether the mismatch is filter/configuration, data, or a genuine issue; report evidence.
22

Client Mission 06 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Please add a dashboard showing leads and appointments.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Create or customize a dashboard and select relevant widgets.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm metric definitions. 2) Open dashboard selector. 3) Add/create dashboard if available. 4) Add lead and appointment widgets. 5) Configure date range/filters. 6) Save. 7) Validate against source records.
EXPECTED RESULT
Dashboard answers the client’s requested questions with correctly scoped metrics.
23

Client Mission 07 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Can you remove the revenue widget? Our team shouldn’t see it.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Widget removal may not be equivalent to restricting revenue data.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Clarify display preference vs data access. 2) Check permissions/data visibility. 3) If dashboard-only, edit dashboard and remove widget. 4) If access restriction, configure appropriate permissions. 5) Test.
EXPECTED RESULT
Revenue is removed from the dashboard if requested, and data access is restricted separately if necessary.
24

Client Mission 08 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“The dashboard is blank.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Could be empty dashboard, filter, permissions, or data issue.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm location/dashboard. 2) Check date range and filters. 3) Look for quick-start/add-widget state. 4) Check if widgets exist in Edit mode. 5) Add widgets only with approval. 6) Verify data availability.
EXPECTED RESULT
Explain why blank and restore/configure widgets as authorized.
25

Client Mission 09 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Make this dashboard easier for our sales team.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Dashboard design request needs user questions and priorities.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Ask what decisions sales needs to make. 2) List metrics. 3) Select appropriate widgets. 4) Arrange priority top-to-bottom. 5) Apply relevant filters. 6) Test with sales user.
EXPECTED RESULT
Dashboard layout supports sales workflow and avoids unnecessary metrics.
26

Client Mission 10 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“I want to compare this month to last month.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Date range/comparison settings.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Open dashboard. 2) Set current month range. 3) Configure comparison period if supported. 4) Check each widget’s own comparison settings. 5) Verify the comparison is displayed.
EXPECTED RESULT
Correct period comparison shown; widget-level overrides are understood.
27

Client Mission 11 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“My coworker sees a different dashboard.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Personal dashboard selection, shared dashboard access, or filters.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Compare dashboard names. 2) Check My Dashboards vs Shared with Me. 3) Compare date ranges and filters. 4) Verify sharing/access. 5) Align dashboard selection if intended.
EXPECTED RESULT
Determine whether differences are expected due to personal dashboard, filters, sharing or permissions.
28

Client Mission 12 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Pin the dashboard we use every morning.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Dashboard pinning request.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Open dashboard selector. 2) Find dashboard. 3) Use pin control if available. 4) Confirm pinned list/order. 5) Test reopening.
EXPECTED RESULT
Dashboard is pinned for the appropriate user context.
29

Client Mission 13 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Our new employee can’t see the dashboard.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Access, user role, account location, dashboard sharing.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm employee user and location. 2) Check role/permissions. 3) Check dashboard sharing/access. 4) Grant only approved access. 5) Test as employee.
EXPECTED RESULT
Employee has approved access without granting unnecessary privileges.
30

Client Mission 14 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Move Conversations above Contacts.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Navigation item reordering.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm custom navigation is enabled/eligible. 2) Open sidebar Edit. 3) Drag Conversations to requested location. 4) Save. 5) Verify scope and client view.
EXPECTED RESULT
Menu order reflects approved request.
31

Client Mission 15 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Rename our menu group to Sales Tools.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Navigation group rename.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm group and desired name. 2) Open navigation editor. 3) Rename group using supported control. 4) Save. 5) Verify all users in scope see intended label.
EXPECTED RESULT
Shared navigation group is renamed; functionality unchanged.
32

Client Mission 16 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“The sidebar looks different after the update.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
UI redesign or Custom Navigation activation.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Identify old/new interface. 2) Check Labs/feature rollout context if authorized. 3) Explain navigation changes vs product function. 4) Use search/All Products/breadcrumbs. 5) Avoid toggling Labs without approval.
EXPECTED RESULT
User can navigate in new UI; no risky feature toggle changed.
33

Client Mission 17 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Please create a dashboard for our owner and a separate one for staff.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Different dashboards or sharing/access needs.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Clarify metrics for each role. 2) Create dashboards if feature available. 3) Configure role-appropriate widgets. 4) Set sharing/access. 5) Test each role.
EXPECTED RESULT
Owner and staff dashboards have suitable content and access.
34

Client Mission 18 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“I can’t access Settings.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
User role or location context.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm location and role. 2) Identify which Settings area. 3) Check permission requirements. 4) Request admin approval if needed. 5) Test approved access.
EXPECTED RESULT
Access issue identified and handled with least privilege.
35

Client Mission 19 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Please switch our team to the new navigation.”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Feature rollout change request.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Clarify agency vs sub-account scope. 2) Review official feature documentation and plan. 3) Preview first where supported. 4) Get approval. 5) Enable at correct scope. 6) Test and document rollback considerations.
EXPECTED RESULT
Navigation rollout is safely applied to approved scope—or prerequisites are reported.
36

Client Mission 20 / 20
Dashboard & Navigation • Realistic client request
CLIENT REQUEST
“Can you audit our GHL account and make a navigation cheat sheet?”
WHAT THIS REALLY MEANS
Orientation/audit deliverable.
YOUR GHL ACTION PLAN
1) Confirm account/location. 2) Inventory sidebar items. 3) Map each feature to team tasks. 4) Note permissions/hidden items. 5) Create quick-reference guide. 6) Validate with client.
EXPECTED RESULT
Client receives accurate, account-specific navigation guide and known limitations.
37

Client communication: acknowledge & clarify
Use when request is vague or may affect shared settings
“Thanks for flagging this. I’ll first confirm which location and user role are affected, then review the current dashboard/navigation setup. Before making a shared or permission-related change, I’ll confirm the intended scope with you so we don’t unintentionally affect other team members.”
38

Client communication: completed work
Report what changed, how it was tested, and what remains
“Completed: [specific change].I verified it by [test/verification]. The change applies to [user/location/scope].No changes were made to [permissions/other locations] unless specifically approved. Please check from your user account and let me know if you would like any further adjustments.”
39

Module 01 practice checklist
Complete before moving to Module 02: Contacts
☐ Identify Agency View and Location/Sub-account View.
☐ Switch to the correct practice location.
☐ Locate Dashboard and identify selector/date range/filter/widget areas.
☐ Explain view mode vs edit mode.
☐ Find a feature using sidebar/search/All Products (where available).
☐ Identify where navigation editing is accessed (if enabled).
☐ Explain why hide/show does not equal permissions.
☐ Explain how you would investigate a blank dashboard.
☐ Complete at least 5 missions in a practice account.
☐ Write a client update after each completed mission.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.

6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.

Standard operating procedure for client requests
1. Clarify the desired outcome, affected contacts/assets, timing, and approval.
2. Locate the exact GHL page and confirm the correct location/sub-account.
3. Inspect current configuration and dependencies; capture baseline.
4. Make the smallest safe change; avoid unrelated edits.
5. Test using a controlled contact/record, preview, or test send.
6. Verify result and review logs/status where available.
7. Tell the client what changed, what was tested, what remains, and any risks.
